questions.q: Report: 'I will come tomorrow,' he said.
questions.a: 'He said (that) he would come the next day.' A wrong answer 'he will come tomorrow' shifts nothing — verb, pronoun, and time-word must all move.

questions.q: 'She ___ me that she was leaving.' said or told?
questions.a: 'told' — 'told' requires the listener object ('told me'); 'said' cannot take 'me' directly. A wrong answer 'said me' is a classic Indian-English slip boards penalize.

questions.q: Report: 'I have finished my work today,' Ravi said to his mother.
questions.a: 'Ravi told his mother (that) he had finished his work that day.' has→had, today→that day. A wrong answer keeping 'has finished' shows partial backshift.

questions.q: Reported speech retells what someone said without quoting them: 'I am tired,' she said → 'She said (that) she was tired.' Three things move together — tense steps back, pronouns ______ to the reporter, and pointing words shift (now→then, today→that day).

Fill in the blank: ______ speech retells what someone said without quoting them: 'I am tired,' she said → 'She said (that) she was tired.' Three things move together — tense steps back, pronouns re-anchor to the reporter, and pointing words shift (now→then, today→that day).
Fill in the blank: The camera moves: direct speech is the speaker's camera; ______ speech is the reporter's camera — everything re-frames. 'I am happy here' → 'He said he was happy there'.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student converts statements direct→indirect with the full three-part shift (tense, pronouns, deictics), choosing said/told correctly ('told' needs an object).
